With 300yds to go, Bill Rice made a brilliant and well timed effort and shot into the lead, which he held to the finish, being followed closely by Duffett and the two Flowers.
In the second event, the 1,320 handicap, Dick Best kept in the front until the finishing straight, when Bill Rice passed him to make a spectacular win.

Bill Rice, when the scratch man caught him, displayed a similar ambition and they were still together on the last lap. George Still was well placed at this time and, knowing the necessity, he speeded-up well for an "old 'un." Rice began to get the better of his argument with Flower and then overtook…
Bill Rice did much better than most of us (including Wally Bayliss) thought he would do, and we can be sure that every one of them did their best.
Evans, the Mitcham A.C. representative, which was increased in turn by Bill Rice, Billy Williams and Joe Flower, Belgrave thus winning very easily.

Bill Rice was never in any danger of being headed by Evans, of Mitcham, and finishing full of running, gave us our second win of the evening by 30yds. in 8 min 34 2-5 sec., quite good time and mainly due to Scrimshaw and Rice, who returned about 2 min. 5 sec and 2 min. 6 sec. respectively.
The Mile Team Race provided Belgrave with an easy win, our men finishing 1, 2, 3, 4, led home by Bill Rice, giving the North Londoners present an idea of the Belgrave strength at a mile.

Bill Rice finished for us an easy winner, thus retaining our unbeaten record of some years standing in this event. The Mile Team Race, which we have always won in recent years, gave us another victory Bill Webb was first man home, followed by Norman Gunn, of Mitcham A.C.

With an extra year or two, some racing experience, and a knowledge of tactics, he may well develop, with Scrimshaw, into one of the fastest in the South Harold Titherley won the 300yds. Handicap, and Bill Rice showed his capabilities by running second in the mile Handicap, off 110, in 4min. 14secs.
The time of the winner, Bill Rice, was 10mins. 2 4-5secs.
He handed over third about six yards behind Hedges to Bill Rice. Bill held the position, but Surrey A.C. came up and Poly H. dropped behind us.
Soon after this, Bill Rice and Joe Flower overhauled Bert and strode out together until ten yards from the tape, when Bill “cracked,” leaving Joe a worthy winner.

Allum is with Bert, followed by Ernie, 39, and Flower, 41......Mitchell, our sixth man, is 54th; Bill Rice finds the hill a very severe test; Webb and Smith are also feeling the strain; Arthur Penny is having a “bad time” and has dropped back to about 150; Bayliss and Chorley are still sticking it gamely in the rear.
Our Bert was here definitely 62nd, Warboys 85th, Allum 97th, Bill Webb 101st, Ernie Duffett 128th, Frank Webb 137th and Bill Rice 182nd. The team score, ignoring individuals, 610.
Bill Rice now carried on the good work and he managed to hang on to third position, although S.L.H. were gradually coming up, having beaten Highgate for fourth place.

Germany last year, and toured America with the Universities team and is, moreover, five or six years the senior of our runners, our repre-sentatives must be congratulated upon their good showing. The mile was another close race, Jack Flower beating Bill Rice by a yard, with Sargant, L.A.C., another yard in the rear.

Williams went first and in a very slow run "half" managed to send Bill Rice away 2 yds. to the good. Evans of Mitcham, however, ran a splendid race and not only gave his side the lead but left Bill Rice high and dry.

Footer finished second in the Open Two Miles team race at Gravesend, scoring 26 points to the 13 of the winners, South London H. Bill Rice ran well to finish fourth. On May 17th, many of our members competed at the Geneva S.C. meeting at Stamford Bridge.

Bill Rice forced the pace throughout, with Norman Gunn his closest attendant until near home, when Joe went by the latter. Thus matters ended all square on the evening, Belgrave, Croydon and Mitcham each scoring 12 points with Epsom 4.

Despite a very fine first leg by Jack Williams we were forced to take second place; but no mistake was made in the mile team race, in which we placed our four men in the first five, with Bill Rice the actual winner.

At the Printing and Allied Trades Sports held at Herne Hill our team was successful for the third year in succession in winning the "Jockey Cup." Our thanks on this occasion are due to Arthur Allum (4), Bill Webb (5), Bill Rice (7),—16 points.
Joe Flower and Bill Rice filled the minor placings and so collected a few more points. A Tie was the result of the High Jump, Fleming, and W.
Championship winning team, ran well and kept off a determined challenge by Bill Rice. Tom Scrimshaw displayed some fine running in the 440 yards Handicap and the final was a great race to watch.
We hear that Belgrave gained their usual easy team win, that Tom Carter was the first man to finish, and that Bill Rice and Harry Shields were prominent on our behalf.
Bill Rice is great, as consistent as the moon, and as varying; sometimes brilliant, sometimes clouded over, but always there. Of Shaw, I do not know much owing to business ties.
Bill Rice and Tommy Carter, both suffering from the effects of the 'flu.

…ther splendid performance, which in my opinion shows the fine team spirit which exists amongst our members, was that of Bill Rice. He was suffering from a very bad throat and should not have run, but as there was no one else to take his place, he did his bit and kept his end up, thereby enabling us…

Here I must award Bill Rice a laurel wreath for tipping the winner, for when the runners had gone into the "country" he remarked to the world at large that it was Footer's day, and certainly "our Bert" had that expression on his face that we in the Club have come to know means "Business only" at the Footer works.

This article would not be complete without some reference to the really remarkable handicap framed by Ernie Duffett. Bill Rice deservedly won but the margin was only two seconds. Another two seconds way three men dead-heated for third place!

Bill Rice now carried on with the good work and by the time he had reached Crawley we were two minutes ahead of the fourth team, and although our prospects of gaining any further places were very remote, so also was the chance of dropping back.

Then came the 1 mile team race and our team, Arthur Allum, Bill Rice, Bill Webb and Tom Cotton was expected to score a win for us. Arthur Allum ran a really magnificent race and holding off Puleston, of Mitcham, won in 4 min. 34 sec.
Following this four —Bill Rice, Carter, Shields and Saunders—came “Young” Jordan, running extraordinarily well, and this lad might well be a champion in the making.

For those who are unable, or not free, to spend a full day in the open, Bill Rice is anxious to arrange some Sunday morning strolls as a supplementary training exercise and a pleasant way to pass the morning.
Flower was 2nd about 50 yards behind, Alf Taylor 3rd another 80 yards further back with "Bill" Rice and J.

Bill Rice (91) was not too happy on the hills, but gave his best "National" performance yet. Tom Carter (95) failed to reproduce his Southern running and must wait another year before doing that which is within his power.
Arthur was setting a fast pace and I knew that my only hope was to keep with him; Bill Rice then fell back and we came across from the Flagstaff, running shoulder to shoulder.

…d done very little over the country but had trained carefully for this race, now did his bit, and after conferring with Bill Rice, who professed to know the exact mileage to all the "pubs" on this stretch, proceeded to lengthen the distance between the three leading clubs, so that our lead was now 2…
Frank Webb "snaked" a win in the High Jump handicap; and Bill Rice gave everyone the opportunity of saying "I told you so!" by easily winning the 2 miles race.
Frost, ran a fine race and deservedly won with Bill Rice second and another Croydon man in W.

Bill Rice went off first for us and, although having a hard race, he managed to hand over a close second behind the Polytechnic H. Corley, of the Poly, went off at a rare pace, but Michael ran with splendid judgment and gradually closed the gap!

…re noticeably prominent—in fact, they held the first dozen places at the end of half-a-mile, but then Harry Shields and Bill Rice decided to move up; Harry led for a while, when Syd Ring ran away cleverly and ultimately finished very fresh 50 yards ahead of Shields, with Tom Carter a similar distanc…

Then another gap and along came a half-dozen together, amongst whom could be seen Martin, the ultimate winner of the handicap, Jack Flower, and Bill Rice who, incidentally, was running in this race nine years ago.

When seen at the end of about a mile and a half the field was led by Close (Reading) followed by a bunch including Cohen (Ashcombe) and Pell (Herne Hill). Our first man was Bill Rice 21st, then Patience 26th, followed by Walker, Duffett, Ring, Webb, F.
Bill Rice again took this stage for us and as the representative of last year's winning team received the letter of greeting from Sir S. Killick, Lord Mayor of London, to Councillor S.
Bain set a very fast pace over the first two laps; and Shaw was lying second after vainly trying to hold on to his man, with Bill Rice still further away, third.

Bill Rice had a nasty fall in the Mile when he seemed all set for a win, but fortunately his injuries have not proved very serious. Scarsbrook beat his club-mate, Nichols, by inches in a stirring finish to the 2 miles event (Captain's Match), and another excellent performance, considering the condit…
Our other three men, Bill Rice, Arthur Allum and Albert Shaw, finished 7, 8, 9, and so we scored 28 pts. to Blackheath H. 38, Mitcham A.C. 51, Poly H. 52, Herne Hill H. 59, and South London H. 72.

In the 1 Mile Team race our men, ably led by our Captain, Bill Rice, kept together in fine style at the head of the field, and although on the last lap Frost, of Croydon, went into the lead with 300 yards and go, Harry Shields raced away and finished in easy winner in time which was very good consid…

The One Mile Team race proved a most exciting race, and the Mitcham boys rose to the occasion in fine style, and although Bill Rice almost ran his heart out in an attempt to force a win, it was not to be, and with Mitcham scoring 1, 5, 6, 7 to our 2, 3, 8, 12, we were one point down on the total points scored to date.

Bill Rice went next and was soon passed by two of his opponents. Bill's lack of speed (due to his team work in distance races; or, perhaps, the sickness which was to strike him down three days later), was soon apparent, but, sticking to his task in fine style, Bill handed over less than 20 yards behind the leaders.
Bill Rice continues to show slow progress, but we are glad to know that his health is improving, even though it will probably be many weeks before he is back to normal.

Harry Shields is our new Track Captain and if only you will support him the same way as some of you used to do Bill Rice, I am sure Harry will think that he is filling Bill's shoes in a manner worthy of his predecessor.
He beat Les in the finishing straight, in time which bettered Bill Rice's win the previous year. The two field events saw us credited with our only win of the evening.

The Two Miles race was won by Bill Webb (N) narrowly from Bill Rice (S). All races were on team and relay principle and gave rise to great interest, and the present existence of Cadogan A.C. may be said to owe something to this meeting.

Harry Hare (who led following Bob Ricketts' death) George Cooper, Bill Rice, George Still, Bert Footer and later the writer were among the "usuals," although at one time or another some hundreds of Belgravians must have enjoyed these strolls.

Our fourth scoring man was the late Bill Rice, who was 13th. This year we had four teams entered, as it is always the club policy to give as many members as possible a chance of representing the Club, and our lads scored an overwhelming triumph.
Bill was placed 3rd in the Club 1 mile track championship in 1929, and the following year finished 2nd in the same event, after a neck-and-neck struggle down the straight with the late Bill Rice.

April 14th was the date and the late Bill Rice was entrusted with the first stretch from Westminster and handed over third. Tom Carter held the position and next Harry Shields set about the opposition to some purpose.
Close support was given by Micky Walker (33) Bill Rice (40) Albert Shaw (43) and Cecil Penny (70) who had been brought into the team at the last moment.
The team was:- BILL MITCHELL (2), ARTHUR PENNY (3), ARTHUR ALLUM (4), BILL RICE (13). Actual winner of this event was LES COHEN , then running in Ashcombe colours and the writer was 97th!

ARTHUR ALLUM (4th), BILL RICE (13th), BILL MITCHELL (2nd), and ARTHUR PENNY (3rd) Winner of the event was none other than LES COHEN, then of Ashcombe A.C.; and our President of today, ALF HARLEY, was 97th.
When Gordon joined the Club in 1934 the Track Captain was one Bill Rice - a good all-round runner - cross-country, track and road relays - also Social Secretary.
